content.value_statement: Azure AI Foundry .NET projects require many clients, packages, and workflow patterns. This skill gives focused SDK guidance for agents, connections, datasets, deployments, evaluations, indexes, and OpenAI clients.
actual_capabilities: Explains package setup for Azure.AI.Projects, Azure.Identity, and preview agent packages.
Shows AIProjectClient authentication with DefaultAzureCredential and a project endpoint.
Guides persistent agent creation, threads, runs, message retrieval, and cleanup.
Summarizes connections, deployments, datasets, indexes, and evaluations APIs.
References versioned agents, OpenAI responses, web search, and Azure OpenAI chat clients.
Lists available agent tools and key SDK types for quick lookup.
limitations: It does not provision Azure resources or grant permissions by itself.
Examples require a valid project endpoint, Azure credentials, model deployments, and connection names.
SDK versions can change after the documented GA and preview versions.
Security and compliance decisions still require tenant-specific review.

use_cases.title: Create Project Clients
use_cases.description: Set up packages, endpoint configuration, authentication, and client selection for a .NET Azure AI Foundry project.

use_cases.title: Configure Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Plan persistent agents, versioned agents, web search tools, thread runs, message handling, and cleanup steps.

use_cases.title: Run Evaluations and Assets
use_cases.description: Use datasets, indexes, deployments, and evaluator configuration to support repeatable project validation.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up the SDK
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new Azure AI Foundry .NET project.
prompt_templates.prompt: I am starting an Azure AI Foundry .NET project. List the required packages, environment variables, and authentication steps for my project endpoint.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Agent Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Build a basic persistent agent workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a persistent agent flow for [task]. Include agent creation, thread setup, run polling, message reading, and resource cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Connect Project Assets
prompt_templates.scenario: Use project connections, deployments, datasets, and indexes together.
prompt_templates.prompt: Map the Azure AI Projects .NET APIs I should use for connections, deployments, datasets, and indexes in [workflow]. Explain the order of operations.

prompt_templates.title: Design Evaluation Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced evaluation planning for production validation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an Azure AI Projects .NET evaluation workflow for [application]. Include dataset inputs, evaluator configuration, deployment selection, run tracking, and result review.

output_examples.input: How do I start using an Azure AI Foundry project from .NET?
output_examples.output: A setup checklist covering packages, endpoint configuration, DefaultAzureCredential, and first client construction.

output_examples.input: Plan an agent workflow that answers user questions and then cleans up resources.
output_examples.output: A step plan for creating an agent, creating a thread, sending a message, polling status, reading messages, and deleting resources.

output_examples.input: How should I evaluate a retrieval workflow in Azure AI Projects?
output_examples.output: Guidance that maps evaluation data, evaluator configuration, deployment names, execution, status review, and result retrieval.

best_practices: Use DefaultAzureCredential and least-privilege Azure RBAC for production access.
Prefer async SDK methods and explicit cleanup for threads, agents, indexes, and datasets.
Keep endpoints, deployment names, and connection names in configuration.
anti_patterns: Do not request credentials with includeCredentials unless the workflow requires secrets.
Do not run cleanup steps against shared resources without checking ownership.
Do not assume preview APIs are stable across SDK upgrades.

faq.question: Can this skill create Azure resources for me?
faq.answer: No. It explains SDK usage. You still need existing Azure resources, permissions, and configuration values.

faq.question: Which SDK versions does it describe?
faq.answer: The source lists Azure.AI.Projects GA v1.1.0 and preview v1.2.0-beta.5.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is usable in Claude, Codex, and Claude Code sessions.

faq.question: Can it help with persistent agents?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers persistent agent clients, threads, runs, messages, polling, and cleanup.

faq.question: Does it replace Microsoft documentation?
faq.answer: No. Use it as a focused guide, then verify final API details against official documentation.

faq.question: What inputs should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide your project endpoint, model deployment name, connection names, and the workflow you want to build.
